Annual rows: panel 1996--2023, same sample in all rows (country-years with every measure), country and year fixed effects, lagged growth, lagged log GDP per capita, human capital, investment, openness, inflation, population growth and commodity terms-of-trade growth; Driscoll-Kraay standard errors (maximum lag 3), confidence intervals from the t distribution with T $-$ 1 degrees of freedom. Five-year rows: non-overlapping averages 1979--2023, same sample in all rows, country and period fixed effects, controls of the conventional specification (log GDP per capita in t\_p $-$ 1, human capital in t\_p and period means of investment, openness, inflation, population growth and commodity terms-of-trade growth), standard errors clustered by country. Tested differences: the six annual measures are stacked and estimated jointly with measure-specific controls and fixed effects (country $\times$ measure and year $\times$ measure); differences tested by wild cluster bootstrap clustered by country (Webb weights, 9,999 replications). The lagged measure and the Hamilton measure are not independent evidence: both use only information up to t $-$ 1 or t $-$ 2 (correlation between them in the annual sample: 0.965). Microstates excluded. * p<0.10, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01.\end{minipage}
